# Lukoil Deep-Dive Analysis

Report 005 | Published 2020-01-05 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-1-5/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/005.json)

Russian oil value, shale fragility and macro expectations.

The inflation and shale-financing directions were successful, while the dollar and oil paths were much less smooth than the base case. The decisive investment weakness was underweighting access risk, not failure to notice it. Domestic Lukoil profitability cannot substitute for the actual ADR holder's recovery.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 005-C01

**Recession risk is elevated over the next year**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | next year |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | heightened risk |
| Asset or variable | US cycle |
| Source blocks | 6, 8, 24 |
| Thesis family | 2019-recession-risk |

A recessionary market collapse followed, but the new pandemic shock prevents treating it as proof that the December industrial and claims pattern would have caused recession.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** Original horizon retained: next year

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [S&P 500 daily closing index](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/SP500) | S&P Dow Jones Indices via FRED | Verified in the audit

Closing prices: January 24, 2020 3295.47; January 27 3243.63; February 19 3386.15; February 25 3128.21; February 28 2954.22; March 2 3090.23; March 23 2237.40. Price index excludes dividends.

- [Fourth quarter and year 2019 GDP, advance estimate](https://www.bea.gov/news/2020/gross-domestic-product-fourth-quarter-and-year-2019-advance-estimate) | BEA | 2020-01-30 | Verified in the audit

Q4 real GDP grew 2.1% annualized, unchanged from Q3; imports decreased but exports increased. Consumption and business investment slowed; 2019 growth was 2.3% versus 2.9% in 2018.

| --- | --- |

Subsequent IMF evidence supports leverage, refinancing stress and weak shale economics. It does not quantify how much supply was caused by cheap capital versus technology and geology.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

### 005-C10

**Weak demand depresses oil prices**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Demand weakens |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Oil |
| Source blocks | 92 |
| Thesis family | oil-demand-price |

EIA attributed the 2020 price collapse partly to a precipitous consumption decline, with storage and contract-expiry effects explaining the negative front-month extreme. This verifies the conditional mechanism, not prediction of that exact shock.

**Direction:** Resolved as stated.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Demand loss combined with storage constraints.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Low liquidity and limited storage pushed WTI futures below zero](https://www.eia.gov/TodayinEnergy/detail.php?id=43495) | Energy Information Administration | 2020-04-27 | Verified in the audit

May WTI futures traded below zero on April 20 amid the demand collapse, expiring contract and limited storage. Positive deferred and other benchmark prices mean this was not all oil trading below zero.

### 005-C11

**Dollar should weaken over coming years**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | next few years |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | base case |
| Asset or variable | US dollar |
| Source blocks | 93 |
| Thesis family | weak-dollar-2020s |

The broad dollar weakened in 2020 and into mid-2021, then rose above the January 2020 level by end-2022. A sustained multi-year weaker-dollar path did not occur over that observable interval.

**Direction:** Early weakness, subsequent reversal.

**Timing:** No precise terminal year given; 2020-22 path disclosed rather than chosen for a binary result.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Nominal broad US dollar index](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DTWEXBGS) | Federal Reserve via FRED | Verified in the audit

Latest-vintage historical observations: 114.9867 on January 3, 2020; 111.3169 on December 31, 2020; 110.5046 on June 1, 2021; 121.4256 on December 30, 2022. Weakness was temporary, not sustained across the following three years.

### 005-C22

**Jurisdiction diversification reduces concentrated policy exposure**

| Field | Assessment |
